Lazio's First-Half Dominance On September 12, 2026 , Lazio started the match with clinical precision, leaving AC Milan struggling to find their rhythm. The breakthrough came early in the 10th minute when Matteo Cancellieri tapped home a cross from Mattia Zaccagni , following a sharp build-up involving Nuno Tavares . The home side looked comfortable, stifling Milan's creative outlets while remaining lethal on the break. The pressure told again in the 39th minute. Tijjani Noslin doubled the lead with a powerful header from close range, sending the home crowd into raptures. At halftime, Lazio appeared to be in total control, while AC Milan 's star-studded lineup, including the veteran Luka Modric , looked disjointed and vulnerable. The ira Turning Point Recognizing the need for change, the AC Milan management made a bold triple substitution at the start of the second half, bringing on Diego ira , Christian Pulisic , and Yunus Musah . The impact was almost instantaneous. In the 65th minute, Pulisic turned provider, delivering a cross that Diego ira met with a sensational left-footed volley to pull one back. Just two minutes later, the comeback was complete. In the 67th minute, Adrien Rabiot fed Diego ira , who unleashed a fierce strike from outside the box to beat Christos Mandas . A tense VAR check followed, but the goal was upheld, leaving the match level at 2-2. AC Milan had wiped out a two-goal deficit in a breathtaking 120-second blitz. A Frantic Finish As the clock ticked down, the intensity rose, resulting in a flurry of yellow cards for Strahinja Pavlovic , Reda Belahyane , and Mattia Zaccagni . Despite AC Milan controlling 66% of the possession and pushing for a winner through late substitute Francesco Camarda , Lazio ’s defense held firm. Late Drama as Torino Fight Back Refusing to capitulate, Torino threw everything forward in the closing stages. Alieu Njie came agonisingly close to scoring in the 75th minute, but his effort rattled the post. As the clock ticked into stoppage time, the home fans were given a glimmer of hope. In the 93rd minute, Che Adams produced a stunning volley from a Gvidas Gineitis cross to make it 1-2. Despite the frantic final moments and a desperate push for an equalizer, AC Milan maintained their composure to secure a hard-fought away win.

Two of Italy's most historic heavyweights met in a tactical battle where patience and late substitutions dictated the rhythm of the match. This Serie A clash drew eyes from around the world to Turin as both sides searched for early-season supremacy. A Cautious Opening Half On September 6, 2026 , Juventus hosted AC Milan in an atmosphere thick with expectation, yet the first 45 minutes were defined by defensive discipline rather than attacking flair. The home side attempted to exert pressure through set-pieces, with Douglas Luiz and Chico Conceicao delivering multiple corners, but the AC Milan defense remained resolute. The flow of the game was frequently interrupted by offside calls against players like Randal Kolo Muani , preventing the Bianconeri from finding a consistent rhythm. AC Milan were equally measured in their approach, focusing on maintaining structure and absorbing pressure. With possession split almost down the middle, neither side could find the decisive pass to break the deadlock before the interval. It was a half of strategic positioning, leaving both managers to look toward their benches for a spark in the second period. Substitution Impact and Stoppage Time Drama The intensity shifted in the second half as tactical changes altered the course of the game. In the 61st minute, AC Milan introduced Alphadjo Cisse and Samuel Chukwueze , a move that paid immediate dividends. By the 68th minute, Chukwueze turned provider, setting up Alphadjo Cisse for a clinical right-footed finish to give the visitors the lead. Juventus responded by bringing on Teun Koopmeiners and later Federico Gatti to bolster their attacking options. Just as it seemed AC Milan would escape with all three points, the match reached a fever pitch in stoppage time. In the 92nd minute, Teun Koopmeiners delivered a perfect cross that found the head of the substitute Federico Gatti , who powered the ball home to level the scores. The match ended in a 1-1 draw, but not before a heated exchange in the final seconds saw both Gatti and Cisse receive yellow cards for unsportsmanlike conduct, highlighting the fierce rivalry between these two giants.
